title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
prompt:
Rebuild a binary tree from its `preorder` and `inorder` traversals (all values unique).

**Example**: `preorder = [3,9,20,15,7]`, `inorder = [9,3,15,20,7]` → `[3,9,20,null,null,15,7]`.

Preorder's first element is the root; its position in inorder splits the left and right subtrees.
hints: Consume preorder left to right with a shared index — each value is the next root.
Find the root's index in inorder; everything left of it is the left subtree, right of it the right subtree.
A value→index map on inorder makes the split O(1) instead of scanning.

solution.explanation: O(n). Preorder gives roots in the exact order we need to build them (root before children), so a single advancing `preIdx` works. Inorder tells us how to partition the remaining range into left/right subtrees — building left first matches preorder's root-left-right order.
